action: Make issues
why: Issues are material: what a session reads and weighs, not orders it must follow.

action: Change an issue: its status, assignee, priority, milestone, release
why: Only one session works an issue at a time, and a proposal is work only once the owner approves it.

action: Claim an issue, let it go or take it over
why: Whoever holds an issue says so, and only the owner takes one from someone else.

action: Rate how risky an issue’s pull request is
why: The session that opened a PR knows what it changes, so it says where reviewing should start; your own rating stands.

action: Remove issues, milestones, releases or docs
why: Taking away what the owner made is their call.

action: Approve, reject or ask for changes to a proposal
why: A proposal asks the owner; deciding it is their answer.

action: Comment, and ask the owner a question
why: Comments are how a session tells the owner what it did, and asks.

action: Write and change docs and releases
why: Docs are material, kept current by the sessions that read them.

action: Make and change milestones
why: A milestone groups issues: material, like the issues in it.

action: Make and change epics
why: An epic is one piece of work across projects (ORR-895): material, like the milestones each project has.

action: Comment on epics
why: An epic is the whole orrery’s, not a board’s (ORR-977): comments on it are held as the epic is.

action: Remove epics
why: Its issues stay where they are; taking away what the owner made is their call.

action: Write presets
why: A preset’s text is an order every later session gets in the owner’s voice: one session writing it would write the orders for the rest.

action: Change the focus prompts and standing instructions
why: The same: what sessions are told must do is the owner’s to write.

action: Change App settings and the statuses
why: They change how orrery runs for every project and session.

action: Ask sessions to focus on an issue, a milestone or an epic
why: Only the owner points sessions at work, so a session can’t set others going.

action: Message a session, or every session
why: A message reaches a session as the owner’s words.

action: Start, stop or give more time to a session
why: Starting work, or ending it, is the owner’s.

action: Connect a repo: open a folder picker on a launcher’s machine
why: It opens a window on your machine, and writes to the folder you choose there.

action: Watch a session in a terminal
why: It opens a window on your machine.

action: Allow or deny what a session asks permission for
why: A permission prompt is there for a person to answer, not another session.

action: Answer in a chat, and ask the owner there
why: A chat is between the owner and its own session.

action: Chat with an agent: start, write in, clear, end or delete a chat, and answer what it asks
why: The chat is the owner talking to an agent, and its requests wait on their answer.

action: Make a schedule that makes issues
why: An issue is material, so a schedule making them is too.

action: Make a schedule that messages sessions
why: Its message would reach sessions as the owner’s words.

action: Make a schedule that starts sessions
why: It starts work as the owner.

action: Make a schedule that moves issues
why: It moves issues as the owner, with no session.

action: Make, change or delete a schedule across projects
why: It runs as the owner on every project it names, and on ones added later.

action: Make an agent’s schedule the owner’s (Make it mine)
why: From then on its words reach sessions as the owner’s, so the owner reads them first: changing it, a pause or a rename, doesn’t make it theirs.

action: Change, run or delete one of the owner’s schedules
why: What the owner set running stays as they set it.

action: Pause or activate all of a project’s schedules
why: Activating all also turns on what was paused on purpose, so it’s the owner’s to do, on Schedules.

action: Ask the owner, on the issue it’s working, to make or change a schedule
why: What a schedule says reaches sessions as the owner’s words, so the owner reads it before it runs (ORR-458).

action: Allow or deny a session’s request for a schedule
why: Allowing saves the schedule as the owner’s, so only they can.

action: Add, rename, remove or invite a person
why: Who works on this orrery is the owner’s to decide.

action: Make or revoke a key
why: A key can’t make or widen a key, so an agent can never become its person. A person handles their own, and the owner issues them to others.

action: Count a use of a feature
why: How often each feature is used, for App settings’ Usage (ORR-881), so what goes unused can go. Only the owner’s own use is counted, and only once they turn counting on; anyone else’s is taken and ignored.

action: End a browser’s login
why: A login is a browser signed in, a phone’s too (ORR-838), so a person ends their own, the owner anyone’s, from App settings: how a lost phone is shut out. Never a session, which has no login and no business with them.

action: Log in or out
why: Nobody has a credential until they’ve logged in, and a session has no use for a login: an agent key signs nothing in.

action: Make a sign-in link for a phone
why: The link signs a phone in as the owner (ORR-837), so only the owner’s own page on this machine makes one, never a session, which would get a login it must never have.

action: Set, change or delete a secret
why: A secret’s value and where it may go are the owner’s to decide.

action: Call an outside service with a secret (egress)
why: orrery fills the secret in, so a session uses a key without ever seeing it.

action: Back up, restore or move the database
why: It decides where all of orrery’s data is.

action: See the repos’ branches, and remove one
why: A branch’s name can hold anyone’s words, and removing one can’t be undone from here.

action: Poll GitHub for pull requests now
why: Each poll spends GitHub’s requests, which are few without a token.

action: Clear the bell or mark it read, or forget a session
why: What waits on the owner goes when they say.

action: Give or change the owner’s name
why: The first to open orrery names its owner; after that, it’s theirs.

action: Make a project
why: A new board belongs to whoever made it, and nobody else is on it until they say.

action: Upload a board's file as a new board
why: A file is untrusted, and a person chooses to bring one in. It never overwrites a board, and nothing in it speaks for anyone.

action: Delete a project
why: It takes everything on the board with it.

action: Add or remove a board’s members
why: Holding a board means saying who’s on it, and agents can’t let themselves in.

action: Import issues into a project
why: What comes in is material, as an issue a session makes is.

action: Upload an image
why: An image is only shown where something links to it.

action: Say what a session is doing, from its hook, channel or launcher
why: It’s a session reporting on itself, which changes nothing on the roadmap.

action: Report an error to the event log
why: Anyone’s page or session can say something went wrong; it’s kept as a report.

action: Mark an event dealt with
why: The log covers every board, so it stays with the owner and their agents.
